$comment: Single source of truth for the ExactMac console design tokens. The .fig is generated from this file by docs/design/build.js, because the app's save_file API path is unreliable and a generated design is reviewable in git diffs. SwiftUI consumes these as semantic colors with per-appearance values.

color.$comment: Semantic names, never gray-NNN. Red is reserved for deny and high-risk emphasis, amber for caution and expiry, green only for an active grant. Light and dark are the same names with different values, which is what makes a single SwiftUI semantic color possible. Every text color meets WCAG AA (4.5:1) on its own scheme's surface AND on surface-raised and surface-sunken, because components place text on all three: Apple's stock #86868B tertiary measures 3.62:1 on white, and #B25000 caution measured 4.37:1 on sunken, so tertiary is darkened to the system label grays and caution to #A04A00. accent FAILED this test as small text on a tinted surface (3.84:1 on sunken), so its two jobs are split: `accent` is a FILL, `accent-text` is INK, and `on-accent` is the label colour that sits on an accent fill. No single blue can do both jobs in dark mode, where the constraint inverts: #3D8BFF gives white-on-fill 3.31:1 but ink-on-raised 4.20:1, and every lighter blue trades one for the other. `on-accent` is dark ink in dark mode, which is why the primary button's label is not hardcoded white. Apple's stock #86868B tertiary measures 3.62:1 and #7C7C81 measures 4.10:1, so tertiary is darkened to the system label grays. separator is a decorative hairline and is deliberately below 3:1; control-border is the one used for interactive edges, which must be perceivable.

space.$comment: 4pt grid. space-1 is the base step; 8 and above are the primary rhythm used for section separation.

type.$comment: Production is SF Pro for prose and Menlo for anything the machine will execute or reported. The .fig is drawn in the design substitutes below because the headless openpencil renderer bundles only DejaVu Sans, Inter and Roboto: it silently substitutes every other family to empty glyphs, so a design using SF Pro cannot be visually verified. Verified-in-renderer beats nominally-accurate-but-unverifiable. The app maps to the production families at build time.

layout.$comment: The approval prompt is 420pt wide. Popover and menu-bar surfaces share the same width so the product reads as one system.
